Vs. 
Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakhho and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque J : Rule Nisi was issued on 21.5.1989 in this case on the respondents to show cause as to why notice dated 18.5.1989 (Annexure-D) issued by the respondent No. 2 should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and of no legal effect 

 2. The petitioner, one of the proprietors of M/s. Nowab Timbers of 488 Purba Monipuripara, Senpara, Rokeya Sharani, Dhaka claims to have been running his timber and saw mills business there after obtaining trade licence etc. from appropriate authorities. While carrying on the said business there the petitioner received a notice dated 11.5.89 on 15.5.1989 from the respondent No.2 to show cause within 7 days why his tin shed structures of 488 Purba Monipuripara should not be demolished as the same was constructed without obtaining sanctioned plan for the same. The petitioner submitted a reply to that notice on 18.5.1989 stating that the said tin shed was not constructed in an area contrary to the Master Plan or development plan and the petitioner is prepared to get sanction for his tin shed on payment of 10 times of the prescribed fee and reasonable fine and prayed for withdrawing the notice of demolition. The petitioner alleges that without giving him an opportunity of personal hearing in violation of the principle of natural justice, the respondents issued notice dated 18.5.1989 directing the petitioner to demolish his tin shed within 3 days. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid notice the petitioner obtained the present Rule Nisi. 

 3. Respondents by filing an affidavit-in opposition controverted the contentions raised by the petitioner stating, inter alia, that since the petitioner constructed the tin shed in question without any sanctioned plan and the petitioner having failed in his reply to satisfy that his tin shed was not liable to be demolished there was no obligation on the respondents to grant the petitioner a personal hearing and his tin shed structure constructed without any sanctioned plan was unauthorised and the respondents committed no illegality in passing the impugned order dated 18.5.1989 for removal of the same. 

 4. Mr. MG Bhuiyan, learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that from the memo dated 18.5.1989 (Annexure' D') it does not appear that the respondents at all considered the reply submitted by the petitioner and the petitioner was given any reasonable opportunity of being heard and the said order for removal of petitioner's tin shed was passed without considering petitioner's reply and without hearing the petitioner and as such the same was wholly illegal inasmuch as the respondents passed the said order not only in violation of the provisions of section 3B (3) of the Building Construction Act,1952. He further submitted that the petitioner received the notice dated 11.5.89 to show cause on 15.5.89 to reply within 7 days of the receipt thereof and as such the petitioner could submit his reply within 22.5.89. But though the petitioner submitted his reply on 18.5.89 the respondents without waiting up to 22.5.89 deprived the petitioner not only the opportunity to be heard but also deprived the petitioner chance to take steps for obtaining sanction for his tin shed on payment of fees and fines as provided in section 3B (3) of the said Act and as such the impugned order is illegal for violating the aforesaid provision of law. He further submitted that without taking resort to section 3A the respondents cannot take resort to section 3B of the Act to remove petitioner's tin shed. 

 5. Mr. Ziaur Rahman Khan, learned Advocate for the respondents submitted that within the Greater Dhaka City area no one is permitted to make any construction of any structure without obtaining a sanctioned plan from the Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipaksha (RAJUK) and as the petitioner failed to show in his reply that he made the construction of the tin shed with sanctioned plan and having indirectly admitted that his tin shed was unauthorised there was neither any obligation nor any necessity to hear the petitioner. Petitioner's tin shed having been constructed in an unauthorised manner without any sanctioned plan the same was liable to be demolished. The petitioner was admittedly served with notice to show cause within 7 days and the petitioner having submitted his reply there was no violation of the provision of section 3B of the Act or of the principle of natural justice in passing the impugned order. He further submitted that since there is no question of improper use of land in this case and since the petitioner constructed the tin shed without sanction the respondents rightly passed the impugned order under section 3B of the Act. 

 (a)	any building has been constructed or reconstructed, or any addition or alteration to any building has been made, or any tank has been excavated or re-excavated, before or after the commencement of the Building Construction (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (Ordinance No. LXXII of 1986), 

 (b) any building is being constructed or re-constructed, or any addition or alteration to any building is being made or any tank is being excavated or re-excavated, without obtaining the sanction under section 3, or in breach of any of the terms or conditions subject to which sanction was granted under that section, he or it may, by a notice, direct the owner, the occupier and the person in charge of the building or the tank to show cause, within such period, not being less than seven days, as may be mentioned in the notice, why- 

 (i) the building or any portion thereof, whether constructed or under construction, as may be specified in the notice, should not be removed or dismantled; or 

 (ii) the tank or any portion thereof, whether excavated or under excavation, specified in the notice, should not be filled up; or 

 (iii) further construction or re-construction of, or addition or alteration to, the building, or excavation or re-excavation of the tank, should not be stopped. 

 (2) Where a person is asked by a notice under sub-section (1) to show cause why further construction or re-construction of, or addition or alteration to, any building or excavation or re-excavation of any tank, should not be stopped, he shall stop such further construction or re-construction or addition or alteration or excavation or re-excavation, as the case may be, from the date the notice is served on him till an order is made under sub-section (3). 

 (3) Where, after considering the cause shown, if any, within the time mentioned in the notice and giving the person showing the cause reasonable opportunity of being heard, or where no cause is shown within such time, the Authorised Officer of the Committee, as the case may be, after such enquiry, as he or it deems fit, is satisfied that the building has been, or is being constructed or re-constructed, or addition or alteration to the building has been or is being made, or the tank has been, or is being, excavated or re-excavated without obtaining the sanction under section 3, or in breach of any of the terms and conditions subject to which sanction was granted under that section, he or it may, by an order in writing stating reasons therefor, direct the owner, the occupier and the person in charge of the building to the tank to remove or dismantle the building or any portion thereof or to fill up the tank or any portion thereof as specified in the order within such time as may be fixed by him or it or to stop further construction or re-construction, addition or alteration or excavation or re-excavation, as the case may be; and otherwise shall make an order vacating the notice. 

 (4) Where further construction or re-construction of, or addition or alteration to, any building, or excavation or re-excavation of any tank has been stopped under sub-section (2) and cause is shown within the time mentioned in the notice against the stoppage of such further construction or re-construction, addition or alteration, excavation or re-excavation, as the case may be, the Authorised Officer or the Committee, as the case may be, shall make his or its order under sub-section (3) within fifteen days from the date the cause is shown. 

 (d) sanction, if prayed for, could not be granted for the construction or re-construction of, or addition or alteration to, the building or excavation or re-excavation of the tank, 

 (ii) makes necessary addition or alteration to the building, or makes the excavation or the filling up of the tank as may be directed by the Authorised Officer or the Committee within the time specified by that Officer or the Committee, and 

 (6) If a person fails to pay the fine or make the addition or alteration or excavation or filling or obtain the sanction as mentioned in sub-section (5) within the time specified by the Authorised Officer or the Committee, as the case may be, under that sub-section, the said officer or the Committee may, by an order in writing, direct the owner, the occupier and the person in charge of the building or the tank to remove or dismantle the building or any portion thereof or to fill up the tank or any portion thereof as specified in the order within such time as may be fixed by him or it. 

 (7) A notice or an order under this section shall be served in the prescribed manner." 

 (ii) issue a notice to the owner or occupier of such building to show cause within 7 days why the same should not be removed or dismantled; 

 (xi) be satisfied that the person failed to pay the fine or to make the addition or alteration or to obtain the sanction under sub-section (5) within the time specified. 

 8. It appears from petitioner's reply submitted on 18.5.89 to the respondent No. 2, Authorised Officer in compliance of the show cause notice dated 11.5.89 that the petitioner prayed for withdrawing the direction for removal or dismantling his tin shed on the grounds that the same has not offended the Master plan or development plan, and the same can be improved, altered or reconstructed with sanction and he is prepared to pay ten times of the prescribed fee and fine imposed for such sanction. It further appears that on 18.5.89 the respondent No. 2 issued the impugned memo (Annexure-D) to the petitioner directing him to demolish his tin shed within 3 days from the receipt of the said order. The impugned order has been written in a form where there is a blank space for mentioning the date of reply to the show cause notice issued to the person concerned. Though the petitioner submitted his reply on 18.5.89 within 7 days of receipt of the said show cause notice on 15.5.89 there is no mention of the said date in the impugned order and the space for the same has not been filled up by mentioning the date of petitioner's reply in that space. Thus it is clear that the respondent No. 2 or the Committee did not at all consider the reply submitted by the petitioner. Had the reply submitted by the petitioner not been placed before the Committee and considered by it there was no reason for not mentioning the date of such reply in the impugned order dated 18.5.89. Thus we find that the Building Construction Committee of the respondent No. 1, Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipaksha in passing the impugned order did not at all consider the reply submitted by the petitioner not to speak of affording any opportunity to the petitioner to be heard. 

 9. Before inserting section 3B and 7 in the Building Construction Act 1952 with effect from 10.11.86 under the memo repealed section 7 of the Act the respondents could not remove any building by using force and they had to apply to the Government for such removal. By empowering the respondents to remove any building or fill up any tank by using force under the newly substituted section 7 of the Act the legislature also vested the respondents with quasi-judicial power under the newly inserted section 3B of the Act to adjudicate into any matter involving removal of any building or part of a building or filling up of a tank. This quasi-judicial power has been vested with the respondents for the purpose of preventing arbitrary use of force by the respondents in removing any building or filling up any tank. The respondents are to pass order for removal of any building after being satisfied that the building in question has been constructed without any sanction or in violation or deviation of a sanction or if there is no sanction the person concerned obtains necessary sanction by paying ten times of the prescribed fee and fine imposed on him. Unless the Authorised Officer or the Building Construction Committee follows the procedure provided under section 3B the order for removal of the building or filling up of the tank will be either illegal or irregular in the facts and circumstances of a given case. 

 10. We have already found that the Building Construction Committee of the respondent No. 1 in gassing the impugned order did neither consider the reply submitted by the petitioner nor afforded any opportunity to him to be heard. We are now to see whether the impugned order is illegal or irregular for lot considering the reply submitted by the petitioner and not affording any opportunity to the petitioner to be heard. We have already noticed from the said reply dated 18.5.89 (Annexure-'C') that the petitioner had indirectly admitted that he constructed the tin shed in question without any sanction and he was prepared to obtain sanction for the same by paying ten times of the prescribed fee and fine imposed on him. But neither the petitioner submitted any plan depositing ten times of the prescribed fee nor prayed for any time to do so nor prayed for any permission for enabling him to apply for such sanction. 

 "From these it is apparent that the petitioner has not showed any cause as to the unauthorised construction but they have prayed for withdrawal of the notice on compassionate ground. In that view of the matter we are of the opinion that the RAJUK (DIT) was not obliged to give any opportunity to the petitioner for further hearing as no hearing was necessary". 

 "It is apparent from the statements made in and papers annexed to the petition that Rajuk caused the notice under section 3B of the Act served on the Masjid Committee the alleged owners and the petitioners and that the petitioners had full knowledge about the notice and made effective representation to the Rajuk against the notice So, by no stretch of imagination it can be said that the petitioners were not notified or were not given an opportunity of being heard as is required by section 3B of Building Construction Act." 

 In this case we have already found that the petitioner indirectly admitted that for his tin shed in question there was no sanction and he was prepared to obtain sanction for the same on payment of ten times of the required fee and fine imposed but he did not submit any application for such sanction of any plan for his tin shed in question. In the above facts and circumstances agreeing with the aforesaid decisions we are of the view that by not considering the reply submitted by the petitioner in compliance of the show cause notice and by not affording an opportunity to the petitioner to be heard the Building Construction Committee acted irregularly and not illegally in passing the impugned order for demolition of petitioner's tin shed as the same was constructed without any sanction in violation of the provision of section 3 of the Act. Under sub-section (5) of section 33 an opportunity has been given to such persons constructing a building without sanction to obtain sanction on payment of ten times of the prescribed fee and fine imposed. Had the petitioner availed of that opportunity to protect his tin shed in question by submitting an application for sanction it could be said that the petitioner was prejudiced for not allowing him an opportunity to be heard to satisfy the Committee about pendency of such an application so as to allow the petitioner time to obtain the sanction to save his tin shed from demolition. In the absence of pendency of such an application for sanction it cannot be said that by non-consideration of petitioner's reply and failure to afford the petitioner an opportunity to be heard there was failure of the principle of natural justice. The provision of section 3B provides for giving seven days' notice to the owner or occupier of building or tank constructed or excavated without sanction to show cause with detailed procedure for passing an order for demolition or filling up embodying the principle of natural justice. In an appropriate case if it is found that Authorised Officer or Building Construction Committee of RAJUK failed to follow the procedure provided under Section 3B of the Act after service of the show cause notice in passing an order for removal of a building or filling up of a tank to the prejudice of any person then such order will undoubtedly be illegal and liable to be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and of no legal effect. But in the present case it cannot be said that the impugned order is illegal. 

 12. As regards the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the Authorised Officer without giving 6 months notice for removal of petitioner's tin shed under section 3A(2) of the Act acted illegally in issuing a notices to show cause within 7 days under section 3B of the Act and in passing the impugned order for removal of the tin shed within 3 days of the receipt of the said order inasmuch as without taking resort to section 3A of the Act the respondents were not authorised to take action for removal of petitioner's tin shed under section 3B and as such the impugned order was wholly illegal and without jurisdiction, it is necessary to examine the provision of Section 3A and the averments made in the petition to decide the same. 

 It is clear that for improper use of land or building contrary to the scheme of land utilisation indicated in the Master Plan the owner or occupier the same may be directed to discontinue such use of such land or building and in the case of a building also remove or dismantle such building under the aforesaid provision of section 3A. It is not the contention of the petitioner or the respondents that the petitioner has been using the land or the tin shed contrary to the scheme of land utilisation indicated in the Master Plan for the area in question. The petitioner categorically asserted in his reply that he is not using the land or the tin shed in question in violation of any Master Plan or deviation of the plan and the respondents in paragraph 8 of their affidavit-in-opposition clearly stated that the impugned order was not passed in exercise of any power under section 3A for improper use of the land but they passed the impugned order for raising the construction in question without sanction from the Authorised Officer. In the absence of any foundation made out in the petition. to invoke the exercise of power under section 3A of the Act it cannot be said that the respondents acted illegally in passing the impugned order in exercise of power under section 3B of the Act without taking resort to in the power under section 3A of the Act and thereby depriving the petitioner longer time to remove his construction. The petitioner's tin shed in question constructed admittedly without any sanction has been directed to be removed by the impugned order. Under section 3A of the Act a building constructed with sanction cannot be used for any purpose other than that mentioned in the sanction. Since the petitioner did not construct his tin shed with sanction no question of improper use of the same contrary to the scheme arises. When a person constructs a residential building with a sanction plan for constructing such a residential building within a residential zone indicated in the Master Plan and starts an industry or business in such building it comes within the mischief of section 3A and his building is liable to be removed if he does not discontinue such improper use. But a person making a construction without violating the Scheme of land utilisation indicated in the Master Plan but without any sanction his building can be removed in exercise of section 3B of the Act. So we find no merit in the contention.
